author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner list treats a page below the first as the first page
summary: Opening the owner list with a page number below the first renders the error page today. It must list the first page of matches instead, for both the unfiltered list and a search by last name.
acceptance_criteria: given the owner list is opened with a page number of zero, when the request is handled, then the first page of matches is listed rather than the error page
given the owner list is opened with a negative page number, when the request is handled, then the first page of matches is listed rather than the error page
given a page number below the first, when the listing is shown, then it reads as the first page rather than as the number asked for
given a search by last name combined with a page number below the first, when the search runs, then the first page of that search's matches is listed
given a page number of the first page or above, when the owner list is opened, then the existing paging behavior is unchanged
non_goals: the veterinarian directory's paging, which is paged the same way but was not part of the reported defect - left as an open question against REQ-VET-001
a page value that is not a number at all
a page number beyond the last page of matches
notes: Bugfix slice. Bar stated in docs/prd.md REQ-OWN-002 done-when bullet 7 and Owner records edge case 4. Two open questions added to the PRD rather than absorbed into this slice.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Boundary normalization of an existing request parameter inside an existing contract. system-design.md Contracts lists OwnerController as owning owner search with paging, and Constants records that page size is a controller-local variable in each listing helper; both stay true. The defect lives in OwnerController.processFindForm, which passes the bound page straight into PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) in findPaginatedForOwnersLastName, so a page below the first produces a negative index and PageRequest.of throws, reaching the error page. Clamping the parameter once on entry to the handler is the request-boundary range check that security-principles.md Trust Boundaries already mandates for external input; no new type, package, pattern, or dependency, and the acyclic package graph is untouched. Grep-resolved (no IDE oracle in this run, the weaker basis): OwnerController.java:95-137 and the identical helper in VetController.java:45-62.
integration_points: processFindForm binds the page request parameter and is the single entry point for the listing; normalize there, once, and thread the normalized value to both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel

addPaginationModel publishes currentPage to owners/ownersList.html, whose first/previous/next links are computed from it; the normalized value is what satisfies the acceptance criterion that the listing reads as the first page, and the template needs no change
the single-match redirect branch and the empty-result rejectValue branch run after the query and stay unchanged, because the clamp happens before the repository call

patterns.description: existing one-based page to zero-based PageRequest conversion; the clamp goes upstream of this call so the index is provably non-negative, rather than catching IllegalArgumentException after the fact

validate type, range, and shape of external input at the boundary; defensive checks belong at the boundary, not scattered through the core - hence one clamp at handler entry, not two inside the helpers

risks.risk: the clamp is mistaken for a business rule added to a web controller, which architecture-principles.md forbids as a fresh violation
risks.mitigation: it is range normalization of a bound request parameter, which the Web controller row's binding responsibility covers; keep it a bare clamp and add no search or paging policy to the controller

risks.risk: VetController carries the structurally identical defect and will diverge from OwnerController after this slice
risks.mitigation: explicit non-goal; already tracked as an open question against REQ-VET-001 in docs/prd.md - do not fold it in

risks.risk: the search test stubs OwnerRepository to return one matching owner in @BeforeEach, so a search for Franklin redirects instead of listing and cannot observe the clamp
risks.mitigation: stub a multi-owner page for the search test, as processFindFormSuccess already does, and assert status 200, view owners/ownersList, and currentPage == 1

notes: No ADR warranted: clamp-versus-reject is already settled as the requirement bar in docs/prd.md REQ-OWN-002 done-when bullet 7 and Owner records edge case 4, leaving no open trade-off for a decision record. No docs/system-design.md update either - the doc carries current state at the contract level and the OwnerController row already reads 'search with paging'; the behavior belongs to the PRD, and Known Defects lists confirmed unfixed behaviors, not ones being fixed in the slice. Testing note: the existing @MockitoBean stub in OwnerControllerTests may be reused for the new tests - docs/testing-principles.md tolerates mock-framework stubs in an already-stubbed class and sanctions MockMvc as the web-boundary harness; do not rewrite the suite. Non-numeric page values stay out of scope. No design-doc-autofix records present, so the autofix audit is a no-op.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: Clamp is normalized once at the processFindForm boundary and threaded through requestedPage into both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, matching the design-block's single-clamp integration point

FIRST_PAGE is a well-named, javadoc'd constant reused both as the clamp floor (Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)) and the one-based-to-zero-based PageRequest offset (page - FIRST_PAGE), replacing a bare magic number
Naming clearly distinguishes the raw bound page parameter from the normalized requestedPage value
./gradlew checkFormat passes clean on the changed files
No new dependencies, types, or exception handling paths introduced; existing error-handling and redirect branches untouched

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Boundary validation strengthened, not weakened: the untrusted `page` request parameter is clamped with Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) before any use, and both call sites (findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel) consume the clamped value — no unclamped path remains in processFindForm

No injection surface added: data access still goes through the derived repository query findByLastNameStartingWith with a bound Pageable; no string-concatenated query text and no request-derived value composing a path or resource name

No output-escaping change: currentPage remains an int model attribute rendered through Thymeleaf's default escaping and the numeric preprocessing in ownersList.html; the clamp can only narrow the rendered value's range
Integer boundary behaviour is safe: Integer.MIN_VALUE clamps to 1 rather than underflowing at page - FIRST_PAGE, which the pre-change code would have wrapped
No mass-assignment change: the OwnerController binder still disallows `id` and `*.id`; no new request-bound type or endpoint is introduced
No secrets, credentials, or connection strings in the diff; the secret sweep over the change set returned only PRD prose about message keys
No supply-chain delta: build.gradle and lockfiles are untouched, so no new dependency and no version change to check against the NVD
Error surface unchanged: the clamp adds no new exception message, so nothing new can reach the error page that renders exception detail

Class sweep for the finding class (unclamped page parameter at the request boundary) across src/main/java found only VetController.showVetList, which is pre-existing surface outside this change set and produces an error page rather than a security-relevant outcome; docs/prd.md already records it as an open question

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The three new tests cover page=0, page=-3, and a search combined with a below-first page, all asserting currentPage==1, but no test exercises a normal page >= 2 (e.g. page=2) to demonstrate the clamp leaves the existing paging offset (page - FIRST_PAGE) unchanged. This is acceptance criterion 5 in prd-entry ('given a page number of the first page or above ... existing paging behavior is unchanged') and design-block risk notes the clamp must not become a business rule. The existing processFindFormSuccess only exercises page=1, which coincides with the clamped floor and cannot distinguish a correct offset from an always-clamped-to-1 implementation.
findings.fix: Add a regression test (e.g. theOwnerListingShouldKeepAnOrdinaryPageUnchanged) asserting model currentPage==2 for a page=2 request, verifying the untouched branch of Math.max still passes the real page through.

approved_aspects: All four new acceptance criteria for page-below-first (zero, negative, search-combined, reads-as-first-page) have dedicated tests
Test names follow the project's BDD naming school (the{Subject}Should{Outcome})
Test data uses meaningful, role-named variables (firstPageOfOwners, firstPageOfFranklins) with no mystery literals beyond the boundary values under test
Mockito stub usage matches the brief's tolerated exception for an already-stubbed collaborator class; no new mocking of internal/domain types

./gradlew test and jacocoTestReport pass green with the new tests included; PageRequest.of would throw on an unclamped negative index, so status().isOk() plus currentPage==1 jointly prove the clamp reaches the repository call, not just the model attribute
Four-phase structure preserved (arrange page stub, blank line, then chained act+assert via MockMvc, consistent with the rest of the suite)

author: change-grader
summary: clamp below-first owner list page to the first page

blast_radius.note: One method in one prod file (12 lines, OwnerController.processFindForm) plus its own test class; two modules are only the prod/test halves of the same owner package, no sensitive paths, no dependency or template change, and the ownersList.html paging links consume currentPage exactly as before.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk: Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) clamps only the low side, both consumers are threaded the clamped requestedPage, page - FIRST_PAGE is arithmetically identical to the prior page - 1, and the empty-result rejectValue and single-match redirect branches are untouched; VetController keeps the identical latent defect, but deliberately, as a recorded PRD open question.

test_adequacy.note: The three new tests do fail against the pre-fix code, since PageRequest.of(-1, 5) throws before the stubbed repository call, so status 200 plus currentPage==1 really proves the clamp; but no test in the entire class ever requests a page above the first, so the suite cannot distinguish the correct clamp from an implementation that always returns page 1, leaving acceptance criterion 5 ('paging at or above the first page is unchanged') unexercised.

reviewer_hedging.note: test-reviewer approved while carrying an unfixed fixable/autofix finding naming precisely that missing page>=2 regression test, and no fix round followed; doc-reviewer first returned changes_requested on a legible-cold bar_clause finding and approved only on a second pass after the PRD wording was reworked.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, consultations, and build retries; the changed files match the design-block primary paths and the prd-entry file targets exactly, the three test names match those declared up front, and both stated non-goals (vet paging, non-numeric page) landed as PRD open questions rather than as code.

rationale: The fix itself reads correct and contained. The residual is test coverage: nothing in the suite requests a page above the first, so an always-clamp-to-1 regression would go undetected, and test-reviewer approved with that exact finding left unfixed. Confirm the gap is accepted, or add the page=2 test before merging.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Fix-pass delta since prior approval is test-only: new test theOwnerListingShouldShowThePageAskedForWhenItIsAboveTheFirstPage and the SECOND_PAGE constant in OwnerControllerTests. No production behavior changed; the OwnerController page clamp is byte-identical to the previously approved version.

Untrusted input path re-walked end to end: the page request parameter is bound as a primitive int by Spring MVC (non-numeric input fails binding, no reflection or expression evaluation), clamped with Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE), then passed to PageRequest.of(page - FIRST_PAGE, 5). No arithmetic underflow or overflow is reachable after the clamp, and the value never reaches a query string, file path, command, or deserializer.

Clamping strictly reduces attack surface versus the prior behavior: page=0 or negative previously produced an IllegalArgumentException surfacing the framework error page (REQ-SYS-002 information-disclosure concern); it now renders the first page.

No injection surface added: the repository call remains the derived query findByLastNameStartingWith with a bound parameter, so the search term stays parameterized and cannot reach SQL as literal text.

Output escaping unchanged: currentPage is an int model attribute and lastName continues through Thymeleaf's default HTML escaping in owners/ownersList; no th:utext, inline JavaScript, or raw writer was introduced.

No secrets in the diff: swept for token, password, secret, key, credential, and datasource wording across all three changed files; only matches are the FIRST_PAGE and SECOND_PAGE identifiers and message-key prose in docs/prd.md.

Supply chain unaffected: the change set touches no build.gradle, lockfile, dependency declaration, or plugin configuration, so no new or upgraded coordinates enter the tree and the previously verified dependency set stands.

Test-only delta introduces no security-relevant test infrastructure: the added import is org.springframework.data.domain.PageRequest, no network, filesystem, deserialization, or credential handling appears in the new test.

Documentation delta in docs/prd.md records the clamp and two open questions; it adds no security claim that the code contradicts, and the non-numeric-page open question is correctly scoped as a requirement gap rather than a live vulnerability.
